note: Two licence grades (Advanced and older Grades I/II were consolidated in the 2009/2010 amendment): the Restricted Grade (entry exam, VU3 call block) gets 50 W DC-input on a limited set of HF segments phone-only (A3E/H3E/J3E/R3E; CW A1A survives only for legacy pre-2009 Grade II licensees) plus VHF/UHF at 10 W; the General Grade (VU2 call block) gets the same HF segments plus CW/digital/image modes at 400 W DC input, 25 W on VHF/UHF, amateur satellite (30 dBW EIRP) and the secondary 5.7 GHz SHF segment. Key deviations: India has no 2200m, 630m, 30m or 60m amateur allocations in the WPC table (those bands are simply absent, so they are omitted here); 70cm is secondary and listed as 434-438 MHz; A3F fast-scan TV is restricted to identification/test transmissions. Ground truth is the WPC O.M. Annexure-I; wpc.gov.in was unreachable from this network so the regulator PDF was taken from the Internet Archive snapshot of 5 Dec 2017, and ARSI (arsi.info) was checked as the society cross-check but publishes no band-plan page.
